youtube.title: Why Your Cat Stares While You Eat (It's Not Judging You)
youtube.description:
A viral theory says your cat thinks you're selfish for not sharing your "kill". The research says otherwise.

Grown cats hunt and eat alone; it's mothers who bring food to kittens. Adult cats barely meow at each other, but they meow at us. Some cats even hide a cry inside their purr that people rate as more urgent. And every dropped crumb teaches the stare that it works. Want a friendlier cat? Try a slow blink.

Sources:
- K. McComb, A. M. Taylor, C. Wilson and B. D. Charlton, 'The cry embedded within the purr', Current Biology 19(13), R507-R508 (2009).
- T. Humphrey, L. Proops, J. Forman, R. Spooner and K. McComb, 'The role of cat eye narrowing movements in cat-human communication', Scientific Reports 10, 16503 (2020).
- J. Bradshaw, Cat Sense (Basic Books, 2013): solitary hunting, meowing directed at people.
- Merck Veterinary Manual, 'Social Behavior of Cats' (accessed 2026-11-20).
- C. Tavernier, S. Ahmed, K. A. Houpt and S. C. Yeon, 'Feline vocal communication', Journal of Veterinary Science 21(1), e18 (2020).
- Partial reinforcement extinction effect: e.g. M. E. Bouton, Learning and Behavior, 2nd ed. (Sinauer, 2016).

How it's made: original 3D characters and scenes, animated by us. The voices are AI voices (ElevenLabs).

Counterphysical: physics that breaks your intuition.
